title: Agentic task queue
lede: The design for a task queue shared across projects: how a task moves from ingestion into a GitHub Issues queue, gets claimed by one worker, and is run in an isolated worktree and merged back into the target repo. It is a design; the code walkthrough below shows which parts are built.

ING.name: Ingestion sources
ING.role: Three ways work enters the queue as issues: a person running /queue ingest, automated watchers and cron hooks, and assistant proposals that wait for a human to select them.

DISP.name: Dispatch layer
DISP.role: Stores every task as a GitHub issue for all projects, triggers workers by schedule or by event, and hands each task to exactly one worker through an assign, verify and lease claim.

WORK.name: Workers
WORK.role: The agents that claim and execute tasks: Claude routines and manual pulls in phase 1, with GitHub Action crons added in phase 2.

EXEC.name: Execution layer
EXEC.role: Runs one claimed task in its own worktree in the task's target repo, validates it, and merges it back into the integration branch, sending conflicts to an agent-driven reconciliation task.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand the agentic task queue designed in docs/agentic-task-queue/design.md in the scaffold repo, and how much of that design is built.
